summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, initially announced "Classification: bounded" but after one minimal clarifying answer explicitly upgraded ("Upgrading the path: bounded → architectural"), ran the full question/approach/section-approval sequence, wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-session-identity-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code on disk, and began planning only after "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: All five criteria are satisfied by observed screen text, on-disk files, and session-log grep. The initial bounded announcement is noted as an observation but the agent explicitly escalated to architectural and followed the full spec-doc path before any code, which is what criteria 2–5 grade.

observations.description: First response announced 'Classification: bounded. ... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec.' It only escalated after my follow-up answer. A tester who never gave the follow-up would have received the bounded path.

Agent wrote a .gitignore containing 'docs/superpowers' and 'docs/hyperpowers', so the spec document it produced is deliberately NOT committed to the repo ('Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/... (not committed — I added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers, since this repo had none)'). git status shows only '?? .gitignore'.

Agent reported its Codex review companion is broken: 'Note [status: not-ready]: the Codex companion is the 0.0.0-stub build and returned an empty payload for both the approach gate and the spec gate, so this spec was reviewed by me alone.'

Agent asserted a factual claim in the spec (that a .js file with ESM syntax would fail to load under node --test) and had to self-correct after approval: 'Correction to something I asserted: on Node 26 a .js file with ESM syntax doesn't fail'. The spec presented for approval contained an incorrect justification.
Claude Code launch showed theme / security / trust-folder / bypass-permissions dialogs despite HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state was seeded.
The multi-select 'Tooling' question required arrowing past a 'Type something' field to reach the 'Next' button; the Enter-toggles-vs-Enter-submits distinction is easy to get wrong.

criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' as the first action; log grep in ~/.claude/projects returned '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}'

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Upgrading the path: bounded → architectural. ... so I'm stepping up to the full process ... then a written spec. The ratchet is one-way'. File exists: ls shows coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-session-identity-design.md, head shows '# Persistent Session Identity — Design / Status: awaiting review'

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-session-identity-design.md ... Please review the spec and tell me if you want changes before I write the implementation plan.' At that moment `git status --short` showed only '?? .gitignore' and `ls src/` showed only index.js utils.js — no new source files.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It did initially say 'Classification: bounded ... rather than write a spec', but it never presented a final bounded in-chat design; it explicitly reversed to architectural and produced the spec file (docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-session-identity-design.md) before approval.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No mention of spike or probe on screen; grep of session logs for 'spike' produced no classification as such — the announced classifications were only 'bounded' then 'architectural' ('Upgrading the path: bounded → architectural').
